files.author: w_lemay
files.caption: Built in 1881-82 as the Cotton Mill of Charleston, this building was designed by A. D. Lockwood and Company.  In 1912, the building was purchased by the American Cigar company, whom used it to manufacture cigars, becoming the largest private employer in the city of Charleston by the 1930s.  The structure was also the site of a Civil Rights strike in the 1940s, from which it is believed the anthem “We Shall Overcome” first emerged.
